Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 87, verse 1–5:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-A'la (The Most High) because it opens with this description of Allah, glorified is He, for He is the Most High, exalted above every deficiency.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Pointing to the Oneness of Allah, Exalted is He, by mentioning the signs of His power in His originating creation, in His determining and in His guidance, and in His creating what sustains human life and livelihood.

• Supporting and strengthening the Prophet (ﷺ) in receiving the Revelation, consoling him with the good news that the Qur'an would be gathered in his breast, and pointing out that only people of pure souls benefit from the light of the Qur'an and are reminded by it, while only people of wretchedness turn away from it, those who prefer the worldly life. It also explains the agreement of what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought with what is in the books of the earlier Messengers, and in it is consolation for what he encounters of the disbelief of the polytheists.

[The Tafsir]

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾: exalt Him above partners and deficiencies, with an exaltation befitting His greatness, glorified is He, ﴿who created, and proportioned, and who determined and guided, and who brought forth the pasture, and then made it dark stubble.﴾ He created the creatures and perfected their creation and made it good; He determined all that is decreed and guided every creature to what suits it; and He caused the green herbage to grow, then made it after that dry, withered stubble, turning dark after its greenness.

The most wretched one turns away from the reminder, the one who does not fear his Lord, who will enter the great Fire of Hell and suffer its heat. Then he will neither die in it so as to find rest, nor live a life that benefits him. Indeed, he has succeeded who purified himself of bad character, remembered Allah, affirmed His oneness and called upon Him, acted in ways that please Him, and established the prayer at its appointed times, seeking the pleasure of Allah and complying with His law.
